subject.title: Feature: inbound 'reply in thread' / 'rit' user directive

question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in inbound natural-language reply-in-thread suffix, and if so what exact trigger vocabulary and `replyToMode` override rules should it use across supported channels?
rationale: Source inspection shows the feature is absent and technically bounded, but trigger words, default-on behavior, optional config, and cross-channel threading overrides are product/API choices rather than a safe automatic repair.

options.title: Approve narrow built-in directive
options.body: Define deliberate trigger phrases, avoid broad bare-word triggers unless explicitly accepted, keep config out unless justified, and document how the directive interacts with each channel's reply modes.

options.title: Keep existing reply controls only
options.body: Treat `replyToMode` and `[[reply_to_*]]` tags as the supported mechanisms and close or decline natural-language suffix parsing as too implicit.

options.title: Defer to broader reply-policy design
options.body: Hold this issue until maintainers design a cross-channel reply-placement policy that can cover user suffixes, tool-use heuristics, and channel-specific thread behavior together.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow built-in directive
recommendation.body: Define deliberate trigger phrases, avoid broad bare-word triggers unless explicitly accepted, keep config out unless justified, and document how the directive interacts with each channel's reply modes.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history signal on inbound finalization and reply-threading policy in the affected core paths.
